Institution of the suit followed by an application under Order 38, rule 5 CPC for an order for furnishing sufficient security by the petitioners 1and 2 and failing which for an order for attachment of the vessel MV Eurco Explorer the carrier of the consignment of the Controller of Movement and Storage, Chittagong, before judgment which was necessary as the petitioner 3 had no property within the jurisdiction of the trial Court except the vessel and if the vessel is allowed to leave the jurisdiction of this court, the decree, if made, will be in executable against the said petitioner. Upon such application the court directed the petitioners to show cause and also by the impugned order passed an ad-interim order of attachment before judgment of MV Eurco Explorer. 

 6. Mr. Mokbul Ahmed, appearing in opposition to this Rule, on the other hand, submitted that the order for attachment and the order for furnishing bank guarantee are independent. He submits that when the vessel after an ad-interim attachment before judgment was released, except the bank guarantee there would be no other asset, in Bangladesh, to satisfy the decree, in case the plaintiff succeeds, and the rule .relating to the order of furnishing of bank guarantee should be discharged. He further submits that the plaintiffs had sufficient cause of action for bringing the suit. 

 It a foreign ship which is calling at international ports on the usual voyage, if comes within the jurisdiction of the Court, shall not ordinarily be treated as a movable property within the jurisdiction of the Court liable to attachment before judgment, unless there are other facts and compelling reasons calling for an action under this rule, apart from over questions of jurisdiction. It In the case of Messers United Venture Navigation Co. Ltd. it was held that where the order of attachment is modified and a new order of furnishing a security bond is passed it is a consequential order dependent on the order of attachment and it stands automatically revoked as a necessary consequence of the setting aside of the order of attachment. In that case, after the ad-interim order of attachment was passed the security bond was furnished for release of the ship from the attachment before judgment. Here before us the ship was released on furnishing bank guarantee. The opposite party contends that the order directing to furnish the bank guarantee is an independent order and there is no error in passing the said order and it does not call for interference by this court. No doubt, the order directing to furnish bank guarantee is an independent order but it is made in consequence of the order of attachment and where the order of attachment itself cannot be sustained in law the consequential order for security has no leg to stand on in law. This view of mine finds support from the decision in the case of Messrs United Venture Navigation Co. Lid. Whether the order made under Or. 38 r. 5 is within the ambit of the provision of law or not is to be seen on the facts of a given case. From the facts of this case I have no hesitation to hold that the order impugned is not attracted at all in that the ship in question cannot be treated as movable property within the meaning of Or. 38 r. 5 CPC. The unreported decision referred to above is also in the same line. It was further contended by the opposite. party that in the event of setting aside the impugned order and consequently to direct return of the bank guarantee the opposite party-plaintiff will have no other remedy for satisfaction of the decree, if made' in the suit. The situation which may arise, as contended by Mr. Mokbul Ahmed, may be resolved by taking recourse to an appropriate forum which is recognised in Private International Law and to meet such situation remedy does not lie under Or. 38, r. 5 CPC. To support this view suffice it to refer the case of Messrs United Venture Navigation Co. Ltd.
